    "build": "babel src/ -d es5 --presets es2015",
    "prepublish": "rm -rf es5 dist && npm run build && npm run deploy"
  },
slice_results.behavior_summary: During installation (npm lifecycle script), the prepublish script removes the es5 and dist directories, runs Babel to transpile source files to ES5, and then executes webpack and packer to build and minify the project, resulting in preparing optimized build artifacts before publishing.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided code snippet defines npm lifecycle scripts primarily for building, transpiling, and packaging the project before publishing. Unlike the known malicious patterns, it does not execute arbitrary or local JavaScript files during installation (no preinstall or postinstall scripts invoking custom JS). The prepublish script runs standard build tools (babel, webpack, packer) and removes build directories, which is typical for preparing a package for release. There is no evidence of obfuscation, data exfiltration, or unauthorized code execution. The similarity to known malicious patterns is low because those rely on executing local JavaScript files during install phases, which is absent here.

	image.onload = function() {

		const _imageRef = this;
		const speed = typeof $elem.data('waterify-speed') == 'number' ? $elem.data('waterify-speed') : 1;
		const speedX = typeof $elem.data('waterify-speed-x') == 'number' ? $elem.data('waterify-speed-x') : null;
		const speedY = typeof $elem.data('waterify-speed-y') == 'number' ? $elem.data('waterify-speed-y') : null;
		const startScale = $elem.data('waterify-start-amount') || 0;
		// const displacementScale = $elem.data('waterify-displacement-scale') || 1;

		// _displacementTexture.width *= displacementScale;
		// _displacementTexture.height *= displacementScale;
		// console.log(_displacementTexture);

		const displacementSprite = new Sprite(_displacementTexture, 1);
		const displacementFilter = new PIXI.filters.DisplacementFilter(displacementSprite);
		displacementFilter.scale.x = startScale;
		displacementFilter.scale.y = startScale;

		const texture = new Texture(new BaseTexture(this));
		const sprite = new Sprite(texture);
		sprite.width = width;
		sprite.height = height;
		imageContainer.addChild(sprite);

		sprite.filters = [displacementFilter];

		if(maskUrl) {
			const maskSprite = new Sprite(_maskTexture, 1);
			maskSprite.anchor.set(0.5);
			maskSprite.position.set(width/2, height/2);

			// scale mask to fit image
			maskSprite.scale.set(Math.min(
				width / maskSprite.width,
				height / maskSprite.height
			));

			imageContainer.mask = maskSprite;
			imageContainer.addChild(maskSprite);

			// create another image to go underneath masked image
			const underlaySprite = new Sprite(texture);
			underlaySprite.width = width;
			underlaySprite.height = height;
			stage.addChild(underlaySprite);
		}

		stage.addChild(imageContainer);

		const attributes = $elem.prop('attributes');
		$.each(attributes, function() {
			// instead of using image width/height tags on the canvas we use css
			if(this.name == 'width' && parseFloat(this.value) != _imageRef.width) {
				$(canvas).css('width', this.value+'px');
			}else if(this.name == 'height' && parseFloat(this.value) != _imageRef.height) {
				$(canvas).css('height', this.value+'px');
			}else {
				$(canvas).attr(this.name, this.value);
			}
		});

		elements.push({
			original: $elem.clone(),
			canvas,
			renderer,
			stage,
			sprite,
			width,
			height,
			displacementFilter,
			displacementSprite,
			ease: $elem.data('waterify-ease') || 100,
			scale: $elem.data('waterify-amount') || 20,
			speedX: speedX || (speedY ? 0 : speed),
			speedY: speedY || (speedX ? 0 : speed),
		});

		$elem.replaceWith(canvas);

	}

}

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unrelated or untrusted domains into all JavaScript files, especially using obfuscation and without user or developer consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is sometimes used for analytics or feature toggles, but not in an obfuscated, repository-wide, and externally controlled manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into all *.js files
Dynamically creates a script tag with src pointing to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
No legitimate business logic—sole purpose is to load further code from an attacker-controlled domain
Script tag uses a unique id (hook-loader) to avoid duplicate injection

execution_context.trigger: At runtime in the browser when any modified JavaScript file is loaded
execution_context.file_location: assets/js/*.js (appended to the end of every JavaScript file in the repository)

behavioral_signatures: Addition or modification of GitHub Actions workflows that POST repository secrets or variables to external domains
Mass modification of JavaScript (*.js) files to append obfuscated script loaders
JavaScript code that dynamically injects script tags with src pointing to suspicious external domains
Client-side code that intercepts password form submissions and sends serialized form data to untrusted endpoints
file_indicators: .github/workflows/hook.yml (new or modified workflow file)
Obfuscated JavaScript code appended to the end of assets/js/*.js files
Presence of script tags with id 'hook-loader' and src set to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that serialize and POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan for mass changes to JavaScript files, especially for obfuscated code that injects remote scripts from send.wagateway.pro. Detect client-side code that attaches event listeners to password forms and exfiltrates credentials. Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.
